question: do the twelve bank members need twelve compiled programs, or do their program-shape axes agree?
instrument: benchmarks/program_shape_census.py --skip-certificate (reads array shapes from logs/exact-operand-cache.npz; nothing is compiled and no MAST profile is rebuilt)

source.metadata_guard: metadata.arm_count == 12, asserted before any row is read
source.identities: six MAST shot/slice pairs (21978/35, 21983/35, 21985/51, 21986/46, 21989/55, 22086/43), each at two arms (pure, mixed)

result.sole_per_row_varying_shape: efit_lcfs, a reference contour at 153/155/147/139/145/151 nodes per identity; it is a receipt operand, not a program argument

geometry_value_agreement.measurement: the persisted operand cache's radius, height and wall arrays were compared across all twelve arms
geometry_value_agreement.reading: the twelve arms carry bit-identical mesh coordinates and wall geometry; the only array that differs across them is flux (max abs difference 0.482), which is a traced operand, so the value-keyed geometry_identity is shared across the twelve rather than distinct

reading.today: the twelve bank members present ONE shape signature and one value digest, so they compile to ONE program today: the per-identity variation lives in traced arguments (external flux, target current), which the program accepts, while the mesh the identity hashes is bit-identical across all twelve
reading.corroboration: docs/figures/millisecond-converged-solve/compiled-slice-cache/receipt.json reports same_cached_program true for all twelve members and cache_reuse_passes 12 on an H200 run independent of this census
reading.correction: an earlier version of this receipt inferred twelve programs from the fact that geometry_identity is value-keyed. That inference was wrong for the bank: it assumed the mesh values differ per member, and the direct comparison shows they do not. The value digest is a compile trigger when the mesh values change, which they do across rungs and across shots whose reconstruction moves the mesh, so capacity-keying remains a lever there, but it is not a bank-local saving
reading.conclusion: for the bank the lever is not a new program key; it is cache persistence and portability, since the same program is recompiled once per runtime-version directory (twelve today) and once per rung whose mesh capacity differs

not_persisted: the solve support cell index list (coordinates.cells) whose LENGTH is a static program shape; it is host-derived per solve and repeats, so a census of it needs the solve coordinates, not this operand cache

cache_inventory.bound_is_per_directory: LRUCache._evict enforces max_size against a single cache directory, and nova configures 8 GiB (nova/jax/config.py:27). Twelve runtime-version keys therefore carry twelve independent bounds: the aggregate ceiling is up to 12 x 8 GiB = 96 GiB, and the observed 18.7 GiB is a sum across twelve directories rather than a reading against one bound
cache_inventory.observed_overshoot: runtime-0745ecebea4cb264e054 holds 8.707 GiB, above the 8 GiB bound: _evict runs while dir_size > max_size - additional_size on each put, so a directory can settle just above the bound once no further put has flushed it
cache_inventory.bound_correction_to_plan: f-msc-program-size-budget records '1907 entries totalling 7.6 GB' for the persistent cache: that figure is one runtime key, not the cache. The installed cache today is 3958 entries / 18.662 GiB across twelve keys
cache_inventory.entries_the_twelve_identities_need: one entry today: the twelve arms are shape-identical and carry bit-identical mesh exactly because they share one program; the four certificate cases need four entries today, one per realised capacity, under the census's 300-cell rung

method: bank rows: array shapes and the mesh values were read from logs/exact-operand-cache.npz (allow_pickle=False); nothing is compiled
the comparison is a direct max-abs-difference over the persisted radius, height, wall and flux arrays, so it measures the inputs the program key hashes rather than the key itself
